tools.name: compare_locations
tools.description:
Score 2 to 10 US locations and say how they differ.

Use this for "which of these is the most walkable", choosing between addresses, or any question that puts places side by side. Give addresses or coordinates, and a label for each if you want the results matched back to your own names.

tools.name: score_many
tools.description:
Score up to 10 US locations in one request.

Use this for a list: properties, branches, listings, sites.

Each location counts as one call against your allowance, so a list of ten costs ten. A location that cannot be resolved is reported in errors rather than failing the request.

tools.name: get_dangerous_corridors
tools.description:
Road corridors where pedestrians were actually killed, from federal crash records.

Source: NHTSA FARS 2022-2024 (PER_TYP=5, INJ_SEV in 4,6). Each corridor carries the road name, the city, the total pedestrian deaths and a per-year breakdown, so a claim can be checked rather than taken on trust.

tools.description:
Search SafeStreets' published research on walkability, street design and pedestrian safety.

Returns the article title, summary, URL and its published questions and answers, so a finding can be quoted and linked rather than paraphrased from memory. 32 articles, each built on named public sources.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_insights · Private data: get_walkability_score, get_dangerous_corridors · Public sink: get_walkability_score, search_neighborhoods.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_insights · Private data: get_walkability_score, get_dangerous_corridors · Public sink: get_walkability_score, search_neighborhoods

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
